item.title: Federal court rejects Trump administration order keeping Michigan coal plant open
item.description:
The Department of Energy overstepped when it ordered an aging coal-fired power plant in Michigan to stay open past its planned retirement date last year, a federal court ruled on Friday. The J.H Campbell plant is one of seven fossil fuel plants around the country that the Trump administration has forced to stay in operation, despite the pollution they cause and the enormous costs of keeping them online. Just before it was about to close last May, Trump’s Energy Department invoked short-term emergency powers under the Federal Power Act to keep the 64-year-old plant running, arguing that the threat of outages, along with the need for more energy to power data centers, constituted an emergency. But the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit rejected that argument , with Appeals Court Judge Cornelia Pillard writing that the emergency statute “is essentially a narrow, last-resort…

item.title: I Tried To Find Out What Republicans Think of Trump's $5,000 Checks. Then I Got Trapped.
item.description:
DALLAS—How did Republicans at the GOP midterm convention feel about President Donald Trump's offer to send every American adult a $5,000 check? I tried to find out. I got very far and also basically nowhere. That's because, upon descending to the floor of the convention—where journalists were typically given access in 15-minute increments to interview attendees—a couple of us were lumped in with the photographer escort. We did not know what that entailed. In practice, it meant we were herded to the front and placed as close as possible to the stage: on the (literal) floor, up against the plexiglass, for Vice President J.D. item.title: BRICS leaders meet in India as wars and US tensions test the bloc
item.description:
Russia’s president landed in India for a BRICS summit that looks set to underline a broader reordering of global alliances. The talks in Delhi — also set to be attended by China’s leader — point to India’s attempt to balance ties with global powers: It has long sought to deepen relations with the US, but is unlikely to meet Washington’s demands to curb relations with Moscow and is reportedly set to propose a strategic economic dialogue with Beijing . They also come amid efforts by several smaller powers to hedge against an unpredictable US: Canada is strengthening ties with European and African nations , Qatar’s prime minister just visited China , and Vietnam’s leader is visiting Russia, France, the US, and Canada this month. — Prashant Rao

item.title: Jimmy Kimmel Didn't Air Talarico Interview Over Fear of FCC 'Equal Time' Threats
item.description:
For the second time this year, James Talarico, the Texas Democratic candidate for the U.S. Senate, appeared on a late-night talk show only to get bumped from the nightly broadcast. In each case, both the hosts and the network seemingly buckled to pressure from President Donald Trump and the Federal Communications Commission (FCC). And just like in that earlier case, it provides a perfect example of why we should abolish the equal time rule. "I'll be interviewing James Talarico tomorrow night under unusual circumstances," Jimmy Kimmel said Wednesday on his ABC talk show. But the TV audience would not see the segment because of fears that by airing it, ABC's affiliates could run afoul of the equal opportunities requirement , better known as the equal time rule.
